title: NCL Mining Sirdar T&S Gr. C — Mock 04
pattern: NCL Mining Sirdar CBT (100 Q · 100 marks · 90 min · no -ve)

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: The correct ratio of chest compressions to rescue breaths during adult CPR is
questions.solution: The standard adult CPR ratio is 30 chest compressions to 2 rescue breaths.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: The 'Acid Mine Drainage' prevention methods include
options: Capping, sealing, and chemical treatment of acid-forming materials
Applying fertilizer to the pit floor
questions.solution: AMD prevention uses capping, sealing, and chemical treatment.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Air gap should be
questions.solution: Minimized.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Amendment of coal mine overburden with
questions.solution: Fly ash and organic matter improve the physical and chemical properties of mine overburden for reclamation.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: The first step to control severe bleeding from a limb wound is
options: Washing the wound with clean water first
Applying firm direct pressure on the wound with a sterile pad
Tying a tourniquet above the heart
Giving the casualty water to drink
questions.solution: Firm direct pressure with a sterile pad over the wound is the first step to control severe bleeding.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: 'Stemming' in blasting refers to
options: The inert material filling the upper part of the blast hole
The detonator placed inside the charge
The primer used to initiate the charge
The sub-drill below the floor level
questions.solution: Stemming is the inert material (e.g., crushed stone or water) used to fill the upper part of the blast hole and confine the charge.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: The 'topsoil substitute' in reclamation may include
options: Composted organic material, mine overburden, and soil amendments
questions.solution: Topsoil substitutes can include composted material, treated overburden, and amendments.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Report writing by Sirdars includes
options: Shift reports on conditions and safety
questions.solution: Shift reports.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: The gas commonly known as 'fire damp' is
questions.solution: Fire damp is chiefly methane (CH4) liberated from coal seams.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: 'Black damp' in mines is a mixture mainly of
questions.solution: Black damp is a mixture of carbon dioxide and nitrogen in which oxygen is deficient.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: The 'gas energy' of an explosive is important for
options: Shattering the rock near the charge
Heaving and displacing the blasted rock
questions.solution: Gas energy provides the heaving force that displaces and moves the fragmented rock.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Expendable Lamp means
options: A lamp that lasts for many years
A lamp used by the mine manager only
A lamp operated by electrical supply
Used for limited period then discarded
questions.solution: Used for limited period.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Working hours for adults per day should not exceed
options: A limit fixed by the contractor
questions.solution: 10 hours including overtime.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: While splinting a suspected fracture, the joints that must be immobilised are
options: Only the joint nearest the heart
The joints above and below the fracture
The joints of the opposite limb
questions.solution: A splint must immobilise the joints above and below the fracture.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: 'After damp', found after a mine explosion, is a mixture mainly of
options: Carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and carbon monoxide
questions.solution: After damp, found after an explosion or fire, is mainly carbon dioxide and nitrogen with some carbon monoxide.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: A 'detonating cord' has a VOD of approximately
questions.solution: Detonating cord typically has VOD of 6000-7000 m/s.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: For an unconscious person who is breathing normally, the recovery position is used to
options: Keep the airway open and allow fluids to drain
Keep the person awake at all times
Prevent movement of a fractured limb
questions.solution: The recovery position keeps the airway open and allows fluids to drain from the mouth.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Safety induction covers
options: Optional after one year of service
questions.solution: Hazards, rules, procedures, PPE.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Protective clothing includes
questions.solution: Shoes, gloves, helmets, vests.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: 'Outbye' refers to
options: The area near the pit bottom
questions.solution: Towards shaft.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: The presence of hydrogen sulphide gas in a mine is recognised by its
questions.solution: Hydrogen sulphide (stink damp) is recognised by its characteristic rotten-egg smell.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Under Mines Rules 1955, 'Potable water' must be provided at
options: Suitable points within the mine and at the surface
questions.solution: Potable water must be provided at suitable points within the mine and on surface.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Flyrock distance depends on
options: Confinement, charge weight, burden, and stemming
questions.solution: Confinement, charge, burden, stemming.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: For a first-degree burn, the recommended first aid is to
options: Apply ice directly on the burnt skin
Cool the area with running water for about 10-15 minutes
Prick the blisters to drain the fluid
Apply oil or butter to the burnt area
questions.solution: Cool the burn with running water for about 10-15 minutes; do not apply ice, oil, or break blisters.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Under CMR 2017, 'Continuous Improvement' in safety requires
options: Regular review and enhancement of safety systems
questions.solution: Safety systems must be regularly reviewed and enhanced.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Carbon monoxide is dangerous in mines because it
options: Has a pungent smell that gives early warning
Combines with haemoglobin far more readily than oxygen and is odourless
Is lighter than air and disperses quickly
questions.solution: Carbon monoxide is odourless and combines with haemoglobin about 200-300 times more readily than oxygen.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Fall protection plan includes
options: Guardrails, safety nets, personal arrest systems
questions.solution: Guardrails, nets, personal arrest.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Under the Mines Act 1952, no person below the age of ___ may be employed in a mine
questions.solution: Under Section 40 of the Mines Act 1952, no person below 18 years of age shall be allowed to work in a mine.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Roll of Workers means
questions.solution: Register of all employed.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Under the Mines Act 1952, overtime work by a person employed in a mine is payable at
options: Double the ordinary rate of wages
One and a half times the ordinary rate
questions.solution: Under Section 33 of the Mines Act 1952, overtime work is paid at double the ordinary rate of wages.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Lead azide serves as
options: Bulk explosive for the main blast
Material that cools the blast area
questions.solution: Primary explosive.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: 'Dozer push' is effective up to
questions.solution: Effective dozer push is economical up to about 100 m.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Overman means
options: Person holding valid Overman competency certificate
Any worker employed in the mine
questions.solution: Valid competency certificate.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: 'Refuge chamber' is
options: An opening cut in the roof for ventilation
A safe haven or refuge station
A roadway driven at a gradient
questions.solution: A refuge chamber is a safe haven where persons can take shelter during an emergency.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Under the Mines Act 1952, an adult worker shall not be required to work for more than ___ days in any one week
questions.solution: Under Section 28 of the Mines Act 1952, no person shall work in a mine for more than six days in any one week.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Return air in ventilation means
options: Air that has passed through working areas
questions.solution: Air from working areas.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Inspector powers include
options: Enter and inspect any mine, take cognizance
Enter mines only with prior permission
questions.solution: Enter, inspect, enforce.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: The 'bench face angle' in opencast mining depends on
options: Rock mass properties, joint orientation, and groundwater
questions.solution: Bench face angle depends on geological conditions, discontinuities, and water.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: The 'dump level' in opencast mining is determined by
options: Dump design, stability, and reclamation requirements
The number of haul trucks available
questions.solution: Dump levels are determined by design, stability, and reclamation needs.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: For a foreign object embedded in the eye, the correct first aid is to
options: Try to remove the object with tweezers
Cover the eye lightly with a clean pad and refer to a doctor without attempting removal
Rub the eye to dislodge the object
Wash the eye forcefully with salt water
questions.solution: Never try to remove a foreign body from the eye; cover it with a clean pad and refer to a doctor.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Firedamp (methane) is explosive when its concentration in air is between about
questions.solution: Firedamp (methane) is explosive in air at about 5-15% concentration.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Stripping balance ensures
options: Equal overburden removal and coal extraction
questions.solution: Overburden removal keeps pace with extraction.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: 'Push-back' is
options: Systematic lateral expansion of the pit
questions.solution: Systematic lateral expansion of the pit.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Training Rules 1966 framed under
options: Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957
questions.solution: Mines Act 1952.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: For a casualty in contact with live electricity, the first step is to
options: Switch off or isolate the supply before touching the casualty
Pull the casualty away with bare hands
questions.solution: Isolate the power supply first; never touch a casualty in contact with live electricity with bare hands.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: 'Priming' places the
questions.solution: Detonator in the explosive charge.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: The 'Vehicle Maintenance Schedule' for opencast mine equipment must be
options: Whenever a breakdown occurs in the equipment
On festival holidays and long shutdowns
Regular and documented per manufacturer specifications
questions.solution: Maintenance must follow regular schedules per manufacturer specs.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Accident investigation aims to
options: Determine root causes and prevent recurrence
questions.solution: Root causes and prevention.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Under the Mines Rescue Rules, 1985, a rescue brigade maintained at a rescue station shall consist of not less than ___ rescue-trained persons
questions.solution: Rule 3(2) of the Mines Rescue Rules, 1985 requires a rescue brigade of not less than 18 rescue-trained persons at every rescue station.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: The sump at the pit bottom is used for
options: Collecting and pumping out accumulated mine water
questions.solution: The sump collects accumulated water at the pit bottom for pumping out.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Sub-drill ensures
questions.solution: Proper breakage at toe.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: VOD of ANFO ranges

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Under the Mines Rescue Rules, 1985, a rescue room must be provided at a below-ground mine when
options: More than 100 persons are ordinarily employed below ground and there is no rescue station within 35 km
More than 50 persons are employed above ground
The mine is located more than 10 km from a railway station
More than 500 persons are employed in the whole mine
questions.solution: Rule 5(1): a rescue room is required where more than 100 persons are ordinarily employed below ground and no rescue station is within a radius of 35 km.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: 'Pilot cut' establishes
questions.solution: Establishes the initial working face.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Safety lamp under CMR 2017 means
options: A lamp approved by the mine manager
Any lamp in the mine area
Any electric torch used in the mine
questions.solution: CMR 2017 defines an approved safety lamp as a flame safety lamp approved by the Chief Inspector.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: A 'safety communication plan' ensures
options: Regular safety information sharing across all levels
A one-time poster display at the mine gate
A monthly report to the head office only
questions.solution: Communication plans ensure regular, multi-directional safety information flow.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: 'Critical pit depth' is reached when
options: Cost of deepening equals additional revenue from coal
questions.solution: When deepening cost equals additional revenue.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: A 'mine plan' in opencast mining shows
options: All working areas, benches, ramps, dumps, and infrastructure
questions.solution: Mine plans show all operational areas including working faces and infrastructure.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: A statutory safety committee in a mine must include
questions.solution: The statutory safety committee includes both workers' and management representatives.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Under CMR 2017, before firing a shot in an opencast working, warning must be given over the entire area within a radius of ___ metres from the place of firing
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 196(2)(b) defines the danger zone as the area within a radius of 500 metres from the place of firing in an opencast working.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Specific charge is
questions.solution: Powder factor.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Training records must be maintained for
options: All persons employed in the mine
questions.solution: All employed persons.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Survey Report includes
options: Topographical data, bench levels, pit limits, volumes
questions.solution: Topography, levels, limits, volumes.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: 'Bench marking' establishes
questions.solution: Reference elevations.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Haul road formation width depends on
options: Equipment size, traffic volume, safety norms
questions.solution: Depends on equipment, traffic, safety.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: The 'air deck' technique in blasting involves
options: Leaving an air gap in the charge column
questions.solution: Air deck technique creates an air gap between charges to improve fragmentation and reduce costs.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: The 'Dump Reclamation Sequence' typically follows
options: Filling the void with domestic garbage
Levelling the surface of the dump
Stabilization, topsoiling, and revegetation in order
questions.solution: Reclamation follows stabilization, topsoiling, revegetation sequence.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: 'Inbye' refers to
options: The area nearest to the working face
The area near the mine office
questions.solution: Towards working face.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: 'Deck charge' means
options: A hole with no charge at all
questions.solution: Multiple charges separated by stemming.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Refuge station must have
questions.solution: Communication, oxygen, water.

questions.subject: General
questions.stem: A alone can complete a job in 12 days and B alone in 6 days. In how many days can they together complete the same job?
questions.solution: A does 1/12 and B does 1/6 of the work per day; together 1/12 + 1/6 = 1/4 per day, so the job takes 4 days.

questions.stem: India's first space tourist was
questions.solution: Gopichand Thotakura flew on Blue Origin's NS-25 mission on 19 May 2024, becoming the first Indian space tourist. Rakesh Sharma (1984) was a professional cosmonaut, not a tourist.

questions.solution: The Quit India Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi on August 8, 1942.

questions.solution: Pratibha Patil was the first woman President of India (2007-2012).

questions.solution: Maharashtra has the highest number of UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India (6, including the 2025 Maratha Military Landscapes serial nomination).

questions.subject: General
questions.stem: Pointing to a man, a woman said, 'He is the brother of the only daughter of my maternal grandfather.' How is the man related to the woman?
questions.solution: The only daughter of her maternal grandfather is her mother; the man is her mother's brother, i.e. her maternal uncle.

questions.subject: General
questions.stem: Choose the grammatically correct sentence:
options: He has been working in the mine since ten years
Neither the overman nor the shot-firer have reported the incident
The inspector asked the manager where the accident had occurred
Each of the workers were given a safety helmet
questions.solution: The correct sentence uses proper tense sequencing: 'asked' takes the past perfect 'had occurred'. 'since' needs 'for', 'neither...nor' takes 'has', and 'each' takes 'was'.

questions.subject: General
questions.stem: The chemical formula for table salt is
questions.solution: NaCl.

questions.subject: General
questions.stem: Antonym of 'Candid' is
questions.solution: Deceitful.

questions.subject: General
questions.stem: The highest gallantry award of India conferred for conspicuous bravery otherwise than in the face of the enemy is the
questions.solution: The Ashoka Chakra is India's highest peacetime gallantry award; the Param Vir Chakra is its wartime equivalent.

questions.subject: General
questions.stem: Mercury is liquid at room temperature because it is
options: A substance in the gaseous state
A metal with low melting point
A mixture of several different metals
questions.solution: Low melting point metal.

questions.subject: General
questions.stem: The Indian Constitution originally had how many articles?
questions.solution: The original Indian Constitution had 395 articles in 22 parts.
